results.name: shared_last_digit_yes
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose last digit matches the shared last digit of a >= 2-example set (all examples end in the same digit); observed > null means people endorse "ends in d" rule extensions more than the model, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose last digit matches the shared last digit of a >= 2-example set (all examples end in the same digit); observed > null means people endorse "ends in d" rule extensions more than the model, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    ld = np.where(np.isnan(ex), np.nan, np.mod(ex, 10))
    same = (np.nanmax(ld, axis=1) == np.nanmin(ld, axis=1)) & (n >= 2)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = same & (np.mod(t, 10) == np.nanmax(ld, axis=1)) & (d > 0)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: dist2_minus_dist1_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets exactly 2 from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets exactly 1 away; observed > null means people favour same-parity neighbours over adjacent numbers more than the model's interval/parity mix predicts.
results.code:
# name: dist2_minus_dist1_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets exactly 2 from the nearest example minus yes rate for targets exactly 1 away; observed > null means people favour same-parity neighbours over adjacent numbers more than the model's interval/parity mix predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m1, m2 = d == 1, d == 2
    if m1.sum() == 0 or m2.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(y[m2].mean() - y[m1].mean())

results.name: opposite_parity_yes_in_parity_sets
results.description: Yes rate for targets of the opposite parity to the examples, among sets of >= 2 examples all sharing one parity; observed < null means the model's interval/noise mass over-predicts yes to parity-violating targets, observed > null means it under-predicts.
results.code:
# name: opposite_parity_yes_in_parity_sets
# description: Yes rate for targets of the opposite parity to the examples, among sets of >= 2 examples all sharing one parity; observed < null means the model's interval/noise mass over-predicts yes to parity-violating targets, observed > null means it under-predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(ex), np.nan, np.mod(ex, 2))
    same = (np.nanmax(par, axis=1) == np.nanmin(par, axis=1)) & (n >= 2)
    m = same & (np.mod(t, 2) != np.nanmax(par, axis=1))
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: lag1_response_autocorr
results.description: Correlation between consecutive responses within a participant (sessions split where trial_index resets, rows ordered by trial_index); observed > null means responses are serially perseverative beyond what the trial-independent model produces.
results.code:
# name: lag1_response_autocorr
# description: Correlation between consecutive responses within a participant (sessions split where trial_index resets, rows ordered by trial_index); observed > null means responses are serially perseverative beyond what the trial-independent model produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, (np.diff(ti) < 0).astype(int)])
    order = np.lexsort((ti, pid))
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()[order]
    p = pid[order]
    same = p[1:] == p[:-1]
    a, b = y[:-1][same], y[1:][same]
    if a.std() == 0 or b.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])

results.name: early_trial_yes_excess
results.description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index < 90 minus yes rate on later trials; observed > null means people say yes more early in the session (a drift the stationary model cannot produce).

results.name: inrange_yes_four_examples
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets lying strictly between the min and max of a 4-example set; observed < null means the model over-fills the span between examples (too much interval generalisation) for large sets, observed > null means it under-fills.
results.code:
# name: inrange_yes_four_examples
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets lying strictly between the min and max of a 4-example set; observed < null means the model over-fills the span between examples (too much interval generalisation) for large sets, observed > null means it under-fills.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = (n == 4) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & (d > 0)
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() else 0.0

results.name: participant_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across participants (sessions split where trial_index resets) of the overall yes rate; observed > null means individuals differ in yes-bias more than the single-parameter-set model allows.
results.code:
# name: participant_yes_rate_sd
# description: Standard deviation across participants (sessions split where trial_index resets) of the overall yes rate; observed > null means individuals differ in yes-bias more than the single-parameter-set model allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, (np.diff(ti) < 0).astype(int)])
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    rates = pd.Series(y).groupby(pid).mean().to_numpy()
    return float(rates.std()) if len(rates) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: far_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets more than 32 away from every example; observed > null means people generalise far beyond the examples more than the model (its far-target floor is too low), observed < null the reverse.

# description: Yes rate for targets more than 32 away from every example; observed > null means people generalise far beyond the examples more than the model (its far-target floor is too low), observed < null the reverse.
